newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end lower on possible peak in cash.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end lower on possible peak in cash.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed lower on ideas that boxed beef and cattle prices may be near a peak and on projections of increased fed cattle supplies into next year, traders said.

Futures were weighed down by ideas the $73 per cwt fed cattle trade and highest boxed beef values in 11 months were close to topping. December paced the early break on sell stops as concern over increased fed cattle supplies into next year added to losses, traders said.
Technical fund selling added to the break in nearbys with stops hit under 67.500 in December, they said.
However, losses were pared by shortcovering late.
Live cattle closed 0.125 to 0.300 cent a lb lower with October off 0.125 at 73.500 cents.
Tom Tippens, CEO of Professional Cattle Consultants Inc., said that it is possible prices are at the top of the market.
"Even though we got the $73 on the live market and even though we put the (boxed) beef up $5, that's the best of the news - that's going to be the top, Tippens said."
He said he expects slaughter rates to climb in October.
"Your hole (in fed marketings) may have occured in the latter part of September," he added.
In live cattle options, volatility was steady. LFG bought the December 66 put/70 call strangle and commission houses sold the February 60 put/70 call strangle, pit sources said.
Losses in feeder cattle futures were pared late when corn futures dipped after posting gains early. But values remained under previous levels following losses in live cattle futures, traders said.
There was scattered buying on the corn decline but selling by Stone Traders put a cap on the market, pit sources added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.19 at $63.79 per cwt.

R.J. O'Brien and Smith Barney notably sold early while locals bought on the scale-down. Cargill Investor Services spread long October feeders/short February live cattle and Merrill Lynch bought November and sold October early, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle closed 0.300 cent a lb lower to unchanged with October off 0.225 at 64.175 cents.
